turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select
the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Reasoning

**Step 1 — Symmetry screen.** SHG requires a non-centrosymmetric (NCS) space group. Candidates like c007 (Rb₈As₈, Pnma-like), c061/c089 (Cs polychalcogenides), c091 (RbBaBr salts), c023, c064 etc. appear centrosymmetric or are wide-gap ionic salts with negligible hyperpolarizability — eliminated. The strong SHG performers in this pool are the diamond-like (zincblende/chalcopyrite-derived) semiconductors, where all cations sit in aligned tetrahedra.

**Step 2 — Chemistry screen (anion polarizability & bond covalency).** For diamond-like materials, |d| scales roughly with anion polarizability and inversely with band gap: Te > Se > S ≫ Cl/Br/O, and P/As-based pnictides (CdGeAs₂-class, d ≈ 100–200 pm/V) beat chalcogenides. Halides (c053, c084–c086, c100), oxides (c023, c068), and borate-sulfides (c040–c045, rigid BS₃ units but wide gap) will have small d. SiC polytypes (c024–c029) have d ≈ 10 pm/V only.

**Step 3 — Identify the winners.**

- **c073 (CdIn₃Te₄As):** a fully tetrahedral zincblende-derived telluride–arsenide. Combining the most polarizable anions (Te²⁻, As³⁻) with a very small gap, this is in the CdGeAs₂/telluride class — expected d well above 100 pm/V. Best of pool.
- **c030 (Cd₄Si₄P₈ = CdSiP₂, chalcopyrite I-4̄2d):** the famous IR NLO crystal with d₃₆ ≈ 85 pm/V. Guaranteed very large.
- **c070 (Cu₃TaTe₄, sulvanite, cubic P-4̄3m):** NCS cubic telluride; Cu-d/Te-p covalency and small gap give very large d₁₄ (sulvanite tellurides are computed/measured near ~100 pm/V).
- **c066 (YCuTe₂, polar hexagonal P3m1-like stacking):** aligned Cu–Te tetrahedra along c, telluride anion → large d, small gap.
- **c056 (Ag₂In₂Ge₂Se₈ ≈ AgInGeSe₄, stannite-type I-4̄):** diamond-like Ag/In/Ge selenide, analog of AgGaSe₂ (d₃₆ ≈ 33 pm/V) with extra Ge–Se covalency — the strongest of the many selenides (beats the Mg–Ga–Se and Li–Zn–Ga–Se series, whose ionic Mg/Li sublattices dilute the response; c080 CsGa₅Hg₄Se₁₂ is a close runner-up).

Final: c073, c030, c070, c066, c056
